classification.ambient_framework: Cantor-series and product-denominator rationality through integral carry recurrences
classification.attribution: Credit Erdős--Straus for the general product-denominator integer-carry rationality criterion. Wang supplies a recent explicit bounded integral-tail-state formulation in fixed binary radix. Credit the local card only for the direct smooth-semigroup prime-power boundary normalization, its all-scale prefix clearing, and its exact #269 specialization.
classification.mathematical_interest: The boundary ordering materially simplifies the exact residual: composite radices {2,6,10,30} and weighted digits are replaced by prime multipliers {2,3,5} and unweighted smooth-number gap counts.
classification.reusable_scope: Tails whose denominator height changes only when one of finitely many prime-power scales is crossed and whose normalized tail has controlled growth.
classification.why_it_matters: It identifies the correct arithmetic throat for #269--exclusion of one particular polynomial-growth integral carry orbit--without presenting a classical rationality mechanism as new.

primary_sources.title: On the irrationality of certain series
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Section 2, Theorem 2.1, especially equation (2.4) and the telescoping proof: under |b_n|/(a_{n-1}a_n) tending to zero, the product-denominator series is rational exactly when an eventual integer relation B b_n = c_n a_n - c_{n+1} exists with a small carry c_{n+1}.
primary_sources.supports: The classical rationality-via-integral-carry recurrence and its telescoping converse.
primary_sources.does_not_support: The finite smooth-semigroup boundary ordering, prime-valued successive multipliers, the exact counts C_j, or any #269 irrationality claim.

primary_sources.title: Positive dyadic density for rational weighted binary expansions
primary_sources.author: Han Wang
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Section 3.1, Proposition 3.1 (printed page 5): for a rational weighted binary expansion, the cleared tail R_N is integral, satisfies R_{N+1}=2R_N-Q(N+1)d_{N+1}, and is linearly bounded.
primary_sources.supports: A recent explicit integral-carry state with polynomial growth in a fixed-radix weighted expansion.
primary_sources.does_not_support: Variable prime radices, the smooth-height boundary normal form, or the local converse based on exponential separation.

mechanism_comparison.classical_product_denominator_form: A rational series value is encoded by integer carries satisfying a first-order affine recurrence; tail smallness controls the carries and telescoping recovers the value.
mechanism_comparison.local_boundary_form: Ordering distinct prime powers makes exactly one height factor change at each step. Removing that new factor yields U_{j+1}=p_j U_j-C_j.
mechanism_comparison.local_converse: Two polynomial-growth solutions of the same prime-multiplier recurrence cannot differ, because a nonzero difference grows by at least 2 at every step.
mechanism_comparison.remaining_throat: For #269, one must rule out the particular polynomial-growth integral orbit; the recurrence itself and finite numerical replay do not do so.
